subject: Renewal: surge-capacity hedge and pricing carveout
messages:
From: Miriam Lowe <miriam@orionenergy.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Orion Energy Procurement <procurement@orionenergy.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal request: surge-capacity uplift and price protection

Hi Evelyn,

Hope you’re well. Our contract is up for renewal in August and we’re planning for a pretty material increase in usage next year tied to our seasonal forecasting window (Q4 is where most of the uplift happens). Current committed throughput is ~2M tokens/month; looking to provision roughly 2.8M–3.0M tokens/month for the next 12 months with the option to step further in year two.

Three asks from procurement and engineering:
- A price-protection clause (price hold) for at least 12 months post-renewal given our budget cycles.
- A mechanism for burst capacity during Q4 without punitive overage rates (we’d consider a committed burst pool or credits).
- A renewal price that reflects some scale discount — procurement is targeting a 15%–20% discount vs today, or an equivalent credit/retainer structure.

We’re happy to discuss longer terms if that helps get to a better unit rate. Attaching our renewal timeline and a short usage export for the account.

Can you propose a short set of options (12/18/24 months) with headline economics and any operational constraints (e.g., Dedicated availability, SLAs, true-up cadence)? We need something to present to our CFO by July 7.

Thanks — Miriam

Miriam Lowe
Head of ML Platforms, Orion Energy
miriam@orionenergy.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: orion_usage_q1-q2.csv (referenced)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Miriam Lowe <miriam@orionenergy.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request: surge-capacity uplift and price protection

Hi Miriam — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. I’ve looped Ben (AE) to scope commercial options and our sales ops team will pull detailed usage trends. Quick high-level options for discussion:

1) 12-month renewal (fastest path)
   - 15% list discount on current unit price
   - 1 month of invoiced credit applied at signing (to offset Q4 ramp prep)
   - Optional one-time purchase of a 20% burst pool at a fixed overage rate

2) 18-month commit
   - 18% discount + price hold for 12 months from renewal effective date
   - Quarterly true-up with pro-rated reconciliation for overages
   - 2-month onboarding/engineering credit to assist with migration to a Dedicated flavor if desired

3) 24-month commit (best unit economics)
   - 20% discount; price hold for 18 months; annual true-up
   - Dedicated capacity option with committed burst buffer and priority routing (capacity subject to availability)

Operational notes:
- Price hold does not extend to 3rd-party infra pass-through increases (we can limit to model/serving unit price).
- Burst pool can be structured as prepaid credits or a committed burst capacity with capped overage rate.
- SOC 2 evidence and audit logs can be bundled for your procurement pack — I’ll attach SOC2 answers and the term sheet (Ben will share the pricing PDF).

Ben, can you prepare a term sheet with headline economics + a one-page mutual action plan showing milestones to PO and delivery? Miriam, if any of the above needs to be shifted (e.g., different cap on overage), flag it and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Miriam Lowe <miriam@orionenergy.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal request: surge-capacity uplift and price protection

Miriam — appreciate the quick context. Attached is a draft pricing term sheet (pricing_term_sheet_v2.pdf) and a proposed mutual action plan in the HubSpot deal. Quick counter-proposal that balances CFO-friendly budget predictability + our capacity constraints:

Proposed (preferred): 18-month commit- Commitment: baseline 2.8M tokens/month (fixed commit)- Economics: 18% discount off current list pricing for committed usage- Price protection: unit price locked for first 12 months; months 13–18 subject to annual review with a floor (no increases above X% — detailed in sheet)- Burst: 1M-token shared burst buffer prepaid (applied as credits) + capped overage rate at a predictable per-token rate for excess usage- Credits: one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 6 weeks' committed spend applied at signing

If Orion wants a steeper discount, we can do 24 months at 20% but require a slightly higher baseline commit (3.0M tokens/month) and a 2-month non-refundable retainer to secure Dedicated capacity.

Next steps:
- If the 18-month looks good, I’ll drop a DocuSign for signature + PO terms and lock in the onboarding credit.
- Can your team confirm expected Q4 peak (tokens/day) so we can size the burst pool? We can also model a monthly amortized credit schedule for budget approval.

Signatures: Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
